title: Stable reduction of curves and stable maps, Part II: moduli of curves and stable compactifications
summary: Planning pass complete at 528 declarations under PROTOCOL section 0 and NODE_BUDGET 300; no declarations are added. All eight geometric stages MC.0–MC.7 and the general pointed moduli key remain partial with explicit remaining work. The plan retains polynomial nodal section coordinates, dual and bidual, arbitrary original-coefficient Hom/Ext calculations, finite two-base tensor comparisons, completed coefficient actions, finite-projective tensor/limit interchange and the actual Hom_R compatible-family comparison. The reusable relative stable-reflexivity interface, two-base completion for arbitrary completed coefficients, completed-ring Hom/Ext, faithful reflection, pointed hull, sheaf descent, arbitrary-base approximation and all stack geometry remain required. All 528 node objects, 268 baseline declarations, 135 requests, 11 source findings, 21 consumer routes and the six-consumer reserved key are preserved. The entire existing suggested Lean file elaborates; 207 inherited geometric prototype omissions remain. Completion concerns this planning pass and its independent review, not mathematical closure.
readme: The reader document research/blueprint/readmes/StableReductionPartII.md specifies conventions, source scope, APIs, tests and unresolved supplier boundaries. Stable maps remain in the parent; no stable-map moduli construction is asserted here.

stages.title: The pointed curve moduli problem
stages.description: For every g,n≥0 with 2g−2+n>0 construct the groupoid-valued moduli pseudofunctor of smooth or stable ordered n-pointed genus-g curves over arbitrary schemes, using the parent’s curve-family objects. Establish base-change coherence and effective descent; keep isomorphism groupoids distinct from their sets of isomorphism classes. Construct the universal family with an arbitrary additional section, including sections at a node or coinciding with an existing mark.

stages.title: The unpointed Deligne–Mumford construction
stages.description: For g≥2 construct the tricanonical Hilbert locus with polynomial (6t−1)(g−1), identify its projective-frame torsor and quotient stack, and prove representability, finiteness and unramifiedness of the diagonal. Import the parent’s infinitesimal automorphism vanishing and compute the obstruction space, algebraize versal deformations and obtain independent node-smoothing parameters. Deduce a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Z of relative dimension 3g−3 with relative normal-crossings boundary. A projective frame is an isomorphism P(f_*ω³)≅P^{5g−6}_S. Its embedded hyperplane line agrees with ω³ up to tensoring by a base invertible sheaf; no linear basis or trivialization of that base line is retained. The canonical relative-polarization locus requires its own relative Hilbert/Isom comparison. Extend locally Noetherian parent cohomology and duality to arbitrary family bases by the separately specified approximation input.

stages.title: Universal curves and the full pointed stable range
stages.description: Identify the universal stable curve over the (g,n)-stack with the (g,n+1)-stack by contraction and expansion, including collision and node charts. Prove the inverse comparison and arbitrary-base-change compatibility. Establish the genus-zero base (0,3), the genus-one base (1,1), and the resulting smooth proper Deligne–Mumford theorem of relative dimension 3g−3+n for every stable pair. Compute M₀,₃, M₀,₄ and its compactification and the unstable rational-tail contraction. Separate the explicit polynomial model over every commutative ring: monic normal forms and regularity, matrix exactness, the ordered cokernel maps to J and its actual dual, residue/scalar correction, coefficient flatness and arbitrary coefficient base change. These local calculations do not replace completed-local or global stable-reflexivity/descent inputs. The natural coefficient comparisons are specified as an algebra equivalence for the ring, a canonical tensor-ring action and an R′-linear equivalence for the dual, with identity/composition and actual residue-quotient transport. Coefficient evaluation and the correction K are separately natural; these adapters do not establish completed-local or family descent. The explicit polynomial section ideal is finitely presented over its node ring, without noetherianity. Under flat ambient R→B, identify the actual extended ideal J·B, its B-linear dual and the quotient by multiplication maps canonically. For noetherian R and any ideal I, compare AdicCompletion I D and AdicCompletion I Q with the actual Hom and quotient over AdicCompletion I R. Flatness and faithful reflection are distinct: reflection requires faithful flatness; localization away from the section makes the residue quotient zero. These are specialized uses of pinned finite-presentation Hom and completion algebra. They do not supply Knudsen relative stable reflexivity over S→R, Proposition6’s two-base completion comparison, pointed completed-local normal forms or arbitrary-family/sheaf approximation. The Appendix has now been read; its Bourbaki citation and Proposition7 exercise remain exact open inputs. The coefficient inclusion is identified with the inherited algebra map, evaluation is A-linear, and the actual ideal projection r↦r−ιev(r) supplies the canonical section splitting and flatness retraction. These statements hold over every commutative coefficient ring and do not assert R-linearity. The ordinary polynomial matrix complex and its transpose now have explicit coordinate proofs, and its two cokernel maps to the actual J and Hom_R(J,R) are specified with their negative second generators. Tensoring these complexes and completed-local or family conclusions remain separate. For every coefficient module M, prove the four alternating matrix pairs remain exact after id_M⊗_A−, using the A-flat actual presentation cokernels rather than assuming M flat. Specify the tensorized cokernel equivalences to M⊗_A J and M⊗_A Hom_R(J,R), with representative, inverse and uniqueness formulas. These supply the polynomial universal-acyclicity calculation; actual Hom/Ext, biduality and relative stable-reflexivity/completion interfaces remain separate. For the actual polynomial model, identify the native ordinary R-bidual evaluation with an equivalence whose inverse sends F to F(incl) in the section ideal; use the native dual-of-reflexive instance for its R-linear dual. Keep this algebraic calculation separate from arbitrary coefficient-module Hom exchange, higher Ext and the relative stable-reflexivity/completion descent. Construct the actual canonical R-linear isomorphisms Hom_R(J,R)⊗_A M≃Hom_R(J,R⊗_A M) and J⊗_A M≃Hom_R(Hom_R(J,R),R⊗_A M) for every A-module M. Use the signed presentation coordinate identities C_Jθ_DU(P_D)=−U(p)U(Ψ) and C_Dθ_JU(P_J)=U(p)U(Φ), with universal transpose exactness. Require naturality for every A-linear coefficient map and the M=A native-unit/bidual specialization. Finite-free resolution/Hom cochain and higher Ext interpretation, the relative stable-reflexivity theorem, two-base completion and all completed-local/family comparisons are independent remaining targets. Instantiate native Hom cochain complexes in R-modules with the alternating Ψ/Φ ideal phase and Φ/Ψ dual phase, and identify degree-zero cycles through the actual signed presentations. Distinguish their zero positive native cohomology from the still required augmented finite-free projective-resolution and Ext comparison. The actual augmented finite-free R-projective resolutions of J and D are now specified and separately checked with native QuasiIso. Their Hom precomposition differentials equal the existing arbitrary-coefficient cochain maps. Next identify the categorical Hom complex and native higher Ext; then apply the exact Appendix/Ile relative stable-reflexivity and two-base completion theorems, pointed completed-local hull, family/sheaf descent and arbitrary-base approximation. The differential equality alone is not an Ext comparison. The actual categorical Hom-complex comparison is now checked, coefficient-natural in every degree and linked to both native Mathlib positive Ext interfaces. Ext_R^{n+1}(J,R⊗_A M)=Ext_R^{n+1}(D,R⊗_A M)=0 for every M without flatness. The next frontier is the exact Appendix/Ile relative stable-reflexivity and two-base completion theorem, then the pointed completed-local hull, family/sheaf descent and arbitrary-base approximation. All MC.0–MC.7 geometric obligations remain. The exact canonical second exchange is now identified as Φ_D,M∘(η⊗id_M)=Θ_J,M. Together with inherited Θ_D,M and both coefficient-universal Ext vanishings, the polynomial model meets all four conditions of Knudsen Appendix Theorem2(1); over noetherian A this gives the source’s relative stable-reflexivity conclusion for J (and symmetrically D). Actual positive Ext into R is separately transported through the native right tensor unit in both Mathlib Ext interfaces. The suggested file does not invent a generic stable-reflexivity predicate. The remaining work is its reusable owner-level formulation, Proposition6’s two-base completion comparison (including Ŝ-module coefficients), pointed completed-local hull, family/sheaf descent and arbitrary-base approximation. All eight stages remain partial. The actual completed coefficient map and its scalar tower, together with the two-base tensor quotient and balancing kernel, are separate prerequisites; the relative stable-reflexivity completion theorem and geometric descent remain open. The native finite nodal quotient comparison is a linear equivalence for every completed-coefficient module when the coefficient ideal is finitely generated. Its proof controls the completion evaluation kernel; comparison with the entire completed rings requires the separately stated completion argument. Establish compatibility of the actual finite two-base tensor equivalences with all quotient transitions and coefficient-module maps. Keep the resulting coherent finite family separate from an inverse-limit comparison and from the ordinary completed-ring tensor comparison. The actual finite tensor diagrams over A and Â now have an A-linear natural isomorphism and native inverse-limit comparison with forward/inverse projections, uniqueness and cone transport. This compares limits of finite tensors only; ordinary tensor commutation with completion and the full relative completion theorem remain distinct required inputs. The completed-action checkpoint adds twenty declarations (five constructions and fifteen promoted API lemmas), fifteen APIs and fifteen tests. It constructs the actual Â-linear finite tensor diagram, its restriction comparison, the A-linear equivalence with the restricted native completed limit, the transported Â-action on the original A-limit with its actual scalar tower, and an Â-linear equivalence with completed-linear projection formulas. All 406 incoming node objects remain identical; ordinary tensor/limit interchange and full two-base relative completion remain open. For finite free completed coefficients N=Fin(r)→Â, the ordinary tensor R̂⊗_Â N is the native limit of G, with explicit finite projections and a proved universal property. If p is finitely generated, the inherited original-base tensor limit, with its transported Â-action, is also identified with this ordinary tensor. No arbitrary-N tensor/limit interchange, injectivity of R̂⊗_A N→R̂⊗_Â N, completion Hom/Ext theorem, Knudsen Proposition6/7, faithful reflection, pointed hull, sheaf descent or arbitrary-base approximation follows. All eight geometric stages remain partial. The ordinary tensor R̂⊗_Â N is now the native limit of G_N for every finite projective completed-coefficient module N, via an explicit finite-free retraction; the lift is independent of the chosen retraction and rank. If p is finitely generated, compose with the incoming two-base finite-tensor limit comparison to identify the original A-limit, with its transported Â-action, with this ordinary tensor. Projection and cone constructions exist for arbitrary N, but their universal property requires a finite-free retraction. No general finitely presented or arbitrary-N interchange, injectivity of R̂⊗_A N→R̂⊗_Â N, relative Hom/Ext completion theorem, Knudsen Proposition6/7, faithful reflection, pointed hull, sheaf descent or arbitrary-base approximation is concluded. All eight geometric stages remain partial. For finite projective Â-coefficients N, Hom_R(L,R̂⊗_Â N) is now Â-linearly equivalent to the native submodule of quotient-level R-linear Hom families (hₙ:L→Qₙ⊗_Â N) satisfying τᵢⱼ∘hⱼ=hᵢ. The inverse assembles actual compatible tensor sections and is R-linear by separation with finite projections; both inverse laws, evaluation equations and contravariant source compatibility are supplied, including typed instances L=J and L=D. This is a specialized adapter of native module limits and linear maps, not a replacement for generic Hom or limit theory. It does not identify Hom over R̂ from a completed section ideal, prove higher Ext comparison, extend tensor interchange to arbitrary Â-modules, or prove injectivity of R̂⊗_A N→R̂⊗_Â N. Knudsen Proposition6/7, reusable relative stable reflexivity, faithful reflection, pointed hull identification, sheaf descent, arbitrary-base approximation and all eight geometric stages remain open. The rigid genus-one triangle locus imposes four smoothing parameters, including its attachment node; a nodal genus-one component has a fifth parameter. Universal-curve induction adds the old-section collision divisors to the inverse image of the old boundary. Transfer of polynomial expansion flatness through formal Proj and beyond locally Noetherian bases has an explicit supplier gap.

stages.title: Clutching, boundary strata and cotangent lines
stages.description: Lift the parent’s gluing operations to separating and nonseparating morphisms of pointed moduli stacks. Prove they are representable finite and unramified, classify boundary divisors by stable one-edge graphs with their automorphism quotients, and compute the conormal node-smoothing line as the tensor product of the two cotangent lines. Construct marking cotangent lines and their forgetful correction. Do not assert that a whole separating clutching map is a closed immersion, or that normal crossings are globally simple. Relative node choices in a smoothing are finite unramified, not generally finite étale. Construct the normalization as a stack, retaining constant graph automorphism quotients. The smoothing conormal has unsigned branch exchange; the integral higher-order parameter and atlas descent contracts remain explicit inputs, and characteristic-zero citations do not establish them over Z.

stages.title: Coarse moduli, projectivity and full level
stages.description: Construct coarse algebraic spaces separately from the stacks. For g≥2 prove projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse space over Z using pluricanonical direct-image nefness and the ampleness lemma. Obtain a finite surjective normal projective scheme cover. Construct smooth-curve symplectic-similitude level N≥3 over Z[1/N], with a fixed pairing component over Z[1/N,ζ_N]; prove representability, regularity, quasi-projectivity, connectedness and dimension 3g−3, and its smooth projective universal curve. Normalize a chosen projective cover for a stable compactification; never declare naive full level on every nodal curve fine. Retain the homogeneous-level multiplier morphism and the exact fixed symplectic subfunctor; forgetting the pairing choice does not identify the two moduli problems. Section-degree positivity uses the generically surjective evaluation image, without special-fibre vanishing on unstable nodal curves. Fix the determinant degree on the single integral parameter family by relative Serre generation/vanishing before applying fibrewise ampleness and fixed-line openness over Z.

stages.title: Hodge determinant and integral Noether comparison
stages.description: Construct the rank-g Hodge bundle and its determinant line on the stable stacks and prove pullback, forgetting and clutching comparisons. For g≥2 construct the integral line isomorphism λ¹²≅⟨ω,ω⟩⊗O(Δ), its base-change compatibility and uniqueness up to the global units ±1 on the universal integral stack. For a generically smooth stable family over an integral noetherian base compute the boundary pullback at a trait as the sum of node thicknesses. An equality in rational Chow groups does not substitute for this integral Picard-group identity. The rational GRR comparison is proved over C and the integral identity follows by torsion freeness and Picard restriction injectivity. Ordered separating Hodge determinants have exchange sign (−1)^(g₁g₂), while an ordered nonseparating residue changes sign when the branches are swapped. Universal ±1 choices can have identical pullbacks in characteristic2.

stages.title: Stable compactifications and Torelli
stages.description: For an integral quasi-projective S over Z or a field with a stable genus-g family (g≥2), produce a dominant finite cover S′→S and a projective integral compactification carrying a stable extension, by retaining the base in a graph closure. Construct the smooth full-level Torelli map and its Cartesian universal-Jacobian comparison, finite fibres with the ±level ambiguity and the genus-two exception. Construct the compactified Torelli map to the minimal Siegel compactification and its Hodge pullback. For maximal variation deduce nefness and bigness of the pulled-back Hodge line, using generic finiteness rather than a globally finite smooth Torelli morphism.

stages.title: Level Picard parameters and consumer interfaces
stages.description: For a fixed genus g≥2, level N≥3 invertible and degree d∈Z define the level-Picard parameter functor and compare it with relative Picᵈ of the universal smooth curve. Keep the fppf-sheafified Picard functor distinct from globally existing line bundles; identify triples only over algebraically closed fields or under the explicit Brauer-obstruction vanishing condition. Export the moduli and family interfaces to the six key-definition consumers, without rebuilding their Hurwitz stacks, mapping-class groups or tautological Chow rings.
